questions.question_text: Round $3.684$ to two decimal places and write it using approximation notation.

options.why: Rounded correctly but used $=$ even though $3.68$ differs from $3.684$.
Rounded up even though the critical digit $4$ is less than $5$.

questions.solution_text:
The critical digit is $4$, so round down.
$3.684 \approx 3.68$

questions.question_text: Round $7.8362$ to two decimal places and write it using approximation notation.

options.why: Rounded correctly but joined the two values with $=$; a rounded value is not exactly equal to the original, so $\approx$ is required.
Chopped off the digits after the second decimal place instead of rounding, ignoring that the next digit $6$ rounds the $3$ up to $4$.
Made both slips at once: truncated to $7.83$ instead of rounding up, and then wrote $=$ instead of $\approx$.

questions.question_text:
A carpenter measures a plank as $1.7283$ m long.
Which is the better way to record the length to two decimal places, and why?

options.text: $\approx 1.73$ m, because a measurement can never be perfectly exact
$= 1.7283$ m, because the ruler gives the exact length
options.why: Treats a physical measurement as exact, but measuring tools always have limited precision.

options.text: $\approx 2$ m, because lengths should always be rounded to a whole number
options.why: Over-rounds to a whole number, discarding precision the task needs.

questions.solution_text:
A measured length is never perfectly exact, so an approximation is appropriate.
$\approx 1.73$ m

questions.question_text: Round $6.997$ to two decimal places and write it using approximation notation.

options.why: Removed the final digit without rounding up when the critical digit is $7$.
Changed the hundredths digit from $9$ to $0$ without carrying into the tenths and then the whole-number part.
Rounded correctly but used $=$ even though $7.00$ differs from $6.997$.

questions.solution_text:
The critical digit is $7$, so round up. Carry through both retained decimal digits.
$6.997 \approx 7.00$
